what: Southern Company is one of the largest US utilities. Through Alabama Power, Georgia Power and Mississippi Power it generates and delivers electricity across the Southeast, and it also owns natural gas utilities serving millions of customers.
customers: Households, businesses and data centre operators in Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi, and gas customers in several states.
money: regulated electricity generation and delivery in three states
moat: Regulated monopolies in fast-growing southeastern states, with rates set by state commissions rather than competitors.
risks: Debt of about $74 billion against under $1 billion of cash
The Vogtle nuclear expansion ran years late and billions over budget
Regulators decide how much of each investment it may recover
Heavy capital spending requires continuous financing
opportunities: Data centre and manufacturing growth in Georgia raises electricity demand
The completed Vogtle reactors now earn a return instead of consuming cash
watch: Georgia load growth from data centres and rate case outcomes.
